title: The Trait Every Great Teacher Shares
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin identifies commitment—full, undivided commitment to one classroom management approach—as the invisible trait that separates great teachers from struggling ones. He argues that teachers who waver on where their boundaries lie, which consequences to use, or how much noise to tolerate broadcast uncertainty that students, even well-behaved ones, instinctively sense and drift into exploiting. This uncertainty, he says, also spreads to parents, who become more prone to complaining and demanding. His prescribed fix is not necessarily SCM specifically, though he advocates for it, but committing fully to one coherent methodology rather than a wavering hybrid of approaches. He frames confidence and decisiveness as communicating leadership that puts both students and parents at ease.

quotes: It’s something lasting, highly influential, and part of who the teacher is. It’s woven into their manner and demeanor.
You see, teachers who are uncertain or dubious about their classroom management approach always struggle.
Students know fear and weakness in their teacher when they see it, even if it lies below the surface. They can smell it from across the playground.
You can be confident and surefooted outside of the classroom and find yourself perplexed and struggling for air within it. Teaching can be especially unforgiving in this way.
You’re better off embracing one methodology than following your own hybrid system or an approach you don’t fully understand.
Which puts them at ease, removes their excitability, and frees them to settle down, settle in, and focus on learning.
